candidates.name: write-good
candidates.profile: Node library with bundled checks; CLI considered separately; exclude custom checks and editor integrations
findings: README documents English passive suggestions. Fixed main module calls passive-voice among default checks; checks can be disabled or replaced.
Main module returns matched text in reasons. CLI prints annotated text and accepts direct text arguments or file inputs; output and argument exposure must be considered.

Current master package metadata says version1.0.8 and MIT; this is metadata, not a verified installed release. Runtime dependency ranges include passive-voice ^0.1.0. Main module eagerly imports other checks even when disabled.
gaps: Exact dependency resolution, licenses and complete selected dependency data paths unreviewed.
No fixed distribution/runtime or passive/active/adjectival synthetic results.
No retention, diagnostics or runtime transmission verification; absence of network calls in one module is insufficient.
candidates.next: Resolve exact runtime dependency graph and inspect passive detection before a bounded synthetic test. Do not execute floating npx or infer all integrations share the library boundary.

candidates.name: Vale CLI
candidates.profile: Local CLI with explicitly selected local rule set; exclude hosted CMS/editor and remote integrations
findings: Official homepage describes MIT open-source CLI and offline operation.
CMS documentation is a hosted service and shows a passive sequence-rule example; that example is not proof a default local CLI installation supplies or runs that rule.
gaps: Exact CLI release and local English passive rule not selected or verified.
No synthetic workflow or selected-rule data-path review.
candidates.next: Identify an official local passive rule and fixed CLI release. Do not count configuration variants or ports as separate qualified products.
